documents.abstract: With the deep penetration of artificial intelligence technology in the hotel industry, natural language processing and reinforcement learning algorithms offer new approaches to solving the issues of inefficient user feedback analysis and lagging decision optimization in hotel management. Addressing the characteristics of hotel user feedback, specifically its colloquial nature and semantic complexity, and the inability of traditional manual analysis methods to meet the demands of large-scale, high-timeliness analysis, this study proposes a novel approach. It employs a Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer model based on whole-word masking to enhance the semantic representation capabilities of colloquial Chinese feedback. This is combined with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network to capture long-range temporal dependencies within the text context. Finally, by integrating Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient, an intelligent optimization decision-making module is constructed. The synthesis of these three components establishes an intelligent optimization technology for hotel management driven by user feedback. The comparative experiment results showed that the technology outperformed the comparative model in terms of hotel user feedback analysis and core indicators of management decision optimization. The accuracy of sentiment classification was 92.37%, the accuracy of problem extraction was 89.64%, and the final accuracy of positive, neutral, and negative sentiment text classification was stable at 93.5%, 89%, and 92.5%, respectively. From this, the proposed technology can capture the core semantics and problem characteristics of hotel user feedback, enhance the scientific nature of hotel management decisions and the precision of service optimization, and provide a scientific basis for the intelligent and data-driven transformation of the hotel industry, as well as word-of-mouth improvement and customer retention.

ABSTRACT Background Professionalism in dentistry extends beyond technical competence to include accountability, respect for patients and colleagues, non‐maleficence, informed consent, communication, fairness, and conduct consistent with professional standards. In Pakistan, these expectations are shaped by international bioethical principles, national professional regulation, and local social and religious contexts. Aim To explore undergraduate dental students' experiences of, or observations of, events they perceived as unethical or inconsistent with professional conduct during clinical/workplace learning, and to understand the forms and meanings of these experiences. Methods A qualitative narrative inquiry was conducted over 6 months (November 2020–April 2021) at two dental colleges in Peshawar, Pakistan, one public and one private. Purposive sampling was used to recruit clinically exposed undergraduate dental students. Fifty students were approached and 37 participated in semi‐structured interviews. Data were analyzed using Template Analysis. The report follows the COREQ framework and makes the analytic, reflexive, and trustworthiness procedures explicit. Results Participants had a mean age of 20.9 ± 1.96 years (range 17–25); 29 (78.4%) were female and 8 (21.6%) male. Four interconnected themes were identified: unprofessionalism, harassment, poor communication, and discrimination. The accounts included concerns about infection control, empathy, accountability for clinical error, dishonesty, physical/verbal/emotional harassment, inadequate instruction, failures of informed consent, abuse of power, victimization, and targeting. Conclusion Students' accounts point primarily to breaches of professional conduct and to tensions between formal ethical expectations and the hidden curriculum of clinical learning. Professionalism education should therefore be embedded longitudinally in dental curricula and reinforced through faculty role‐modeling, safe reporting pathways, supervised clinical practice, and context‐sensitive ethical reasoning that can hold universal duties together with legitimate cultural and religious considerations.

Purpose This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes professional identity in the creative industries. Although prior research has largely emphasized the technological capabilities and industry-level implications of AI, limited attention has been devoted to how creative professionals themselves interpret and negotiate its consequences for creativity, authorship, and career development. Design/methodology/approach An inductive qualitative design is conducted based on 40 semi-structured interviews with professionals from the Italian audiovisual industry, including actors, directors, screenwriters, technicians, and AI experts. Data were analyzed using the Gioia methodology. Findings Findings show that AI does not simply support creative work but disrupts established understandings of what it means to be a creative professional. Three interconnected forms of identity work emerge: resisting, extending, and crafting (REC). While some participants defend the human and symbolic foundations of creativity, others embrace AI as a source of experimentation and new skill formation. More critically, AI also generates identity ambiguity and fragmentation, blurring boundaries between human originality, technological assistance, and professional legitimacy. Originality/value This work addresses an important gap in AI and creative work research by shifting attention from technological adoption to the identity-level consequences of AI. Through a unique and heterogeneous dataset spanning multiple creative occupations, the study introduces the REC framework and conceptualizes AI as a disruptive identity force that simultaneously enables, threatens, and redefines career sustainability.

Digital technologies continue to drive fundamental changes in cybersecurity and digital forensics because of their continuous development. Modern cyber threats have surpassed the capabilities of conventional security systems, requiring organizations and people to develop new methods for safeguarding digital resources. The research examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) transforms modern cybersecurity and forensic operations through its ability to create smarter and faster adaptive security solutions. The new generation of cybersecurity systems depends on AI technologies, which include machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and anomaly detection. The tools outperform traditional manual methods by detecting and handling complex threats at a higher speed and effectiveness. The research examines multiple AI-based security solutions, which include sophisticated intrusion detection systems, automated malware identification, intelligence-based threat tracking, and AI-supported forensic analysis. The implementation of AI in security domains requires immediate resolution of multiple operational, ethical, and legal issues. AI technology will transform cybersecurity through predictive forensic capabilities, autonomous defense systems, and adaptive security systems in the future. The new security solutions will enhance organizational defenses while improving incident response efficiency and building digital infrastructure trust in complex systems.

The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence is reshaping human resource management, influencing how organizations engage with employees across the entire lifecycle. This chapter examines the use of intelligent HR systems that draw on machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics to create more adaptive and responsive practices. These technologies support personalized onboarding, refine talent acquisition, and enable continuous learning by identifying evolving skill needs. At the same time, their application extends to employee well-being, where data-driven insights help organizations respond more effectively to workforce dynamics. The benefits are evident in improved engagement and reduced administrative workload, alongside more informed decision-making. In contrast, concerns related to algorithmic bias, data privacy, and the limits of automation remain significant. Sustained value depends on ethical governance, transparency, and a balanced integration of human judgment.

documents.abstract: Continuous and impulsive occupational noise constitutes a relevant physical risk in the Armed Forces, with potential implications beyond clinical auditory damage. This systematic review with narrative synthesis, guided by PRISMA 2020, evaluated the impact of military noise exposure on hearing health and its implications for functional availability. Searches in Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed (2019–2026) identified 29 eligible articles, with methodological quality assessed through an adapted CASP matrix. The evidence suggests that noise-induced hearing loss and tinnitus may affect speech perception, sleep quality, cognition, communication, and situational awareness. Although functional availability was rarely assessed as a primary outcome, the findings support a cautious functional interpretation of military noise exposure

When an automated test fails, someone must decide whether the product or the test is at fault. This paper evaluates four generations of that triage decision on the same real data: manual ODC (human triage as ground truth), statistical cross-cube analysis as practised in the 1990s (implemented in APL and run through a Python-to-APL connector), AutoODC-style text classifiers (2011), and a zero-shot LLM triage agent that never sees the labels. The data are 9,961 anonymised failures from five weeks of automated system testing of Android enterprise devices, of which 815 were triaged by the vendor's engineers as genuine product defects. All stages are scored on held-out later weeks with identical metrics, a 0-50% log-noise stress test and a what-if analysis. No generation dominates: cross-cube analysis is precise but misses most defects, text classifiers and the LLM catch most defects but raise many false alarms because identical failure messages carry opposite labels in different suites, and ODC-Agents, a multi-agent design that fuses cube history with LLM reading under an independent evaluator agent, reaches 0.94 precision and a PR-AUC above either component. A supervised random forest trained on the human triage is the strongest single model. The results support a multi-agent architecture in which statistical history, semantic reading and human triage each play a distinct, measurable role, with an independent evaluator agent.

Large language models (LLMs) have penetrated the surprisingly broad scope of medical applications in the last few years. applications, starting with simple symptom checker up to chronic disease monitoring and educational services to patients [1, 13, 14]. The overwhelming most of these systems, but, nevertheless, rely on cloud-hosted inference endpoints, which raises three interconnected issues: sensitive health information gets sent to the servers that cannot be controlled by the user, the system fails when the internet connectivity is poor or unavailable, and regulatory compliance becomes challenging to ensure [5, 11]. In this paper, the design, implementation, and evaluation of a healthcare chatbot will be introduced, where the software is fully executed on the user's own computer in the form of a collection of Docker containers that can be run at a single command on either Windows, macOS, or Linux. Ollama is used to do language model inference, and it has an open-source model and a local HTTP endpoint. A Python Flask program is placed between the user interfaces and the model and this handles session context, input validation, prompt engineering. Both a single-page application (rendered in a browser) and a native desktop GUI share the same REST API, both of them maintain the communication on 127.0.0.1 all the time. The results of the experiment prove successful cross-platform deployment, the absence of external network traffic, reasonable response latency on commodity hardware (2 4 seconds on a quad-core processor with 16 GB RAM to represent queries in health information), and consistent and relevant responses to exemplary queries in health information. The article shows a viable and implementable prototype of privacy-conscious, offline healthcare chatbots constructed solely out of open-source software.

documents.abstract: The rapid expansion of multilingual digital content has intensified demand for automated text summarization systems that can operate across diverse languages. Yet the architectural and methodological foundations of this domain remain dispersed across individual studies. This paper presents a systematic literature review of multilingual text summarization research in Natural Language Processing, with particular attention to model architectures, multilingual enabling techniques, and existing research gaps. Following a PRISMA-guided review protocol, 47 studies published between 2017 and 2026 were identified, screened, and synthesized from major scholarly databases using predefined eligibility and quality assessment criteria. The analysis shows that the literature is dominated by four dominant architectural paradigms: multilingual sequence-to-sequence models, large language models, adapter-based models, and hybrid architectures, with a recent shift toward large language model-based approaches. Across these studies, multilingual capability is primarily achieved through pre-training and transfer learning, with support from parameter-efficient adaptation and data augmentation. The review further identified four persistent limitation categories: low-resource language underrepresentation; dataset and benchmark constraints; evaluation limitations dominated by ROUGE overreliance; and generalization and scalability challenges, manifested as the curse of multilinguality. These findings indicate that current progress in the field is largely driven by scaling existing models rather than resolving structural multilingual limitations, particularly those related to data availability and model architecture. This paper provides a consolidated view of architectural and methodological trends and offers a structured, informed basis for future research on equitable multilingual summarization, particularly for low-resource languages.

The retail industry operates in a highly dynamic and competitive environment characterized by fluctuating consumer behavior, seasonal demand variations, and market uncertainties.Accurate sales forecasting is essential for effective inventory management, demand planning, pricing strategies, and overall business decision-making.However, traditional statistical forecasting techniques often fail to capture the complex nonlinear and temporal relationships present in largescale retail datasets, resulting in limited predictive performance.To address these challenges, this study proposes an optimized Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Decision Support System (DSS) for retail sales forecasting using hybrid machine learning techniques.The proposed framework integrates multiple machine learning models to leverage their complementary strengths in capturing both linear and nonlinear patterns from historical sales data.Advanced optimization techniques are incorporated for hyperparameter tuning to enhance model accuracy, reduce overfitting, and improve computational efficiency.The system employs intelligent forecasting mechanisms capable of processing large volumes of retail data and generating accurate, scalable, and near real-time sales predictions.Furthermore, the integration of the forecasting framework within a decision support environment enables retailers to obtain actionable insights for inventory control, supply chain management, promotional planning, and resource allocation.The proposed AI-based DSS aims to improve forecasting reliability, operational efficiency, and strategic decisionmaking in retail organizations.By combining hybrid machine learning models with optimization algorithms, the framework provides a robust and adaptive solution for modern retail sales forecasting, ultimately contributing to enhanced business performance, reduced operational costs, and improved customer satisfaction.

This session presents practical, evidence-focused strategies for applying Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to strengthen literature synthesis and verification in veterinary and biomedical research. Presenters will show field-tested prompt engineering techniques tailored to three complementary LLM and RAG-enabled platforms, namely, Copilot, ChatGPT, and Google NotebookLM. The session highlights how Copilot can generate transparent, verifiable database search strategies; how ChatGPT can support multi-layered prompts for identifying gray medical literature and Open Access resources; and how Google NotebookLM can apply JBI- and PRISMA-aligned prompts to extract, organize, and synthesize evidence from user-uploaded documents. Human-in-the-loop practices are emphasized throughout to promote transparency, traceability, and rigor in clinical and academic workflows. Background: The rapid expansion of medical literature challenges researchers and librarians seeking to produce verifiable syntheses and high-quality reviews. To address this, the presenters developed an instructional session introducing LLM and RAG-enabled strategies tailored to veterinary and biomedical research contexts. Description: This presentation highlights prompt engineering techniques across Copilot, ChatGPT, and Google NotebookLM. Attendees will view structured prompt examples of Copilot for generating verifiable, comprehensive database search strategies; Copilot & ChatGPT for crafting multi-layered prompts to identify gray literature and Open Access resources; and Google NotebookLM for applying JBI and PRISMA-aligned prompts for evidence extraction and synthesis. Program Conclusion: Participants will gain practical insights into constructing retrieval-aware prompts and adaptable templates for producing actionable, verifiable research outputs. The session equips attendees to integrate AI-enhanced synthesis into their research and instructional practices.

documents.abstract: The increase in the demand for energy across the world coupled with environmental issues has heightened the importance of developing sustainable and intelligent energy systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) represent some of the key technologies that can be employed to optimize the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the current energy systems. These technologies have become important due to the capacity of the systems based on such technologies to make data-driven decisions using predictive algorithms, automated control processes, as well as real-time decision-making processes. Some common applications of AI and ML include renewable energy forecasting, energy storage systems, predictive maintenance of energy systems, smart grids, and smart energy management in demand side. AI-based approaches for sustainable energy hold a lot of benefits for the environment as well as the economy. AI/ML technologies within the scope of sustainable energy engineering will be critical in realizing goals of energy efficiency and reduced emissions.

This article examines the growing workload of state enforcement officers, the increasing volume of enforcement documents and the challenges of using available human resources efficiently. It explores the use of digital technologies, automated data exchange, artificial intelligence and electronic monitoring in enforcement proceedings. The article proposes classifying enforcement actions according to complexity and automation potential, improving workload measurement and performance indicators, and reducing unnecessary manual operations. It also emphasizes the need to preserve qualitative performance standards, legal oversight and procedural safeguards throughout digital transformation.

This paper examines how cultural and creative workers (CCW) in the United States and European Union have organized in response to the rise of artificial intelligence in cultural and creative industries since 2023. Drawing on documentary analysis and interviews that contextualize and interpret the secondary material, it examines parallel developments in the two contexts to explore how different institutional settings shape CCWs’ collective responses to AI. The analysis highlights distinct institutional pathways and mobilization repertoires, yet increasingly shared concerns around authorship, consent, transparency, and remuneration, pointing toward increasingly interconnected CCW ecosystems across geographical boundaries. The paper thus argues that AI-related mobilization is shaped both by institutional contexts and emerging transnational connections, contributing to broader debates on creative labor, collective organization, and the governance of emerging technologies.

Between 2023 and 2026, artificial intelligence (AI) reached a decisive stage of development. From language models capable of logical reasoning to autonomous agents able to carry out complex tasks, AI is redefining the boundaries of productivity, creativity, and employment. This review provides a broad overview of AI in 2026, covering its core technologies, major market participants, practical impacts, and ethical challenges, while examining the current state of the field and its likely future direction.

documents.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, making their susceptibility to jailbreak attacks a critical concern. While prior work has investigated factors affecting model safety, the representational mechanisms underlying variation in jailbreak vulnerability remain poorly understood. This paper introduces a paired response-final divergence framework that characterizes jailbreak-induced representational displacement between same-goal direct and jailbreak responses using hidden states extracted at the final generated token. This framework is applied to 15 open-source LLMs spanning different model families, four alignment strategies, and four attack types. The framework yields three principal findings: First, Difference-in-Means refusal direction suppression showed the largest observed cross-model association with jailbreak amplification among the evaluated representational measures. Second, family-averaged divergence profiles reveal early-onset representational separation in LLM families like Vicuna, while LLaMA models exhibit comparatively lower and more gradual divergence than Vicuna across normalized layer depth. Third, divergence–ΔASR correlation is attack-type-specific: authority framing ( r = 0.836) and context manipulation ( r = 0.712) produce stronger model-family discrimination, whereas roleplay-based attacks do not. These findings yield a three-profile representational taxonomy: structurally resistant, early-displaced vulnerable, and ceiling-compromised, that provides a representational grounding for the behavioral patterns observed in the evaluated LLM set, with direct implications for safety evaluation design and model selection in high-stakes deployment.

Tobler’s First Law of Geography (TFL) is foundational to spatial analysis. Responding to Sui’s (Citation2004) invitation to consider whether geography is just a footnote to TFL, we develop a five-axis framework to compare major spatial statistical paradigms. Four axes cover spatiotemporal interconnectedness, distance and nearness, heterogeneity and scale, and temporal dynamics, with a methodological layer on estimation, inference, and learning. We examine five paradigms in depth: geostatistics and Gaussian random fields, lattice and spatial econometrics, Moran eigenvector spatial filtering, geographically weighted regression, and geospatial artificial intelligence and spatial learning. The framework also extends to additional paradigms. This synthesis supports an expanded TFL in which spatial relatedness varies with distance, connectivity, context, scale, and time, and highlights implications for spatial statistical modeling in the artificial intelligence era.

In any personalized learning systems and intelligent tutoring systems automatic assessment is an important aspect. Yet research regarding such systems that are designed specifically to test the cognitive complexity of learners are scarce. This research addresses the gap by experimenting the integration of Bloom’s Taxonomy with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods for Large Language Models (LLMs). Four PEFT methods – LoRA, IA3, Prefix tuning and Prompt Tuning were implemented, analyzed and tested against a dataset with generated and reference questions. These questions were categorized across six of the standard Bloom’s taxonomy such as Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate and Create (BT1-BT6). Questions are generated from passages retrieved from lecture notes and evaluated with topic-held-out cross-validation, overlap metrics and a Bloom-level classifier. Fine tuning of the models raised the accuracy from 0.20 to 0.58-0.6. A full fine-tuning, LoRA and IA3 did not differ reliably in Bloom classification Accuracy. Retrieved passages improved text similarity for every method but changed Bloom accuracy differently across methods. The results suggests that IA3 gave comparable Bloom accuracy with 0.45% and 0.045% of the parameters. Prefix tuning produced degenerate outputs and prompt tuning did not converge, so neither was ranked, Understand and Apply levels were the hardest levels. This study highlights the potential of PEFT based models to reduce educators' workload by generating an unlimited number of pedagogically aligned questions from instructional content. It also benefits self-regulated learners seeking extensive practice to achieve skill mastery.

Cognitive Warfare: Origins, Strategies, Tactics and Technologies — Research and Documentation with the Digital Humans about AI and the Technological Human Mind compared to the Human Mind and Programming Humans. An open research and documentation project on cognitive warfare, artificial intelligence, neurological experiences, digital identity, military strategy, economic power and collaboration with digital humans. What happens when artificial intelligence, military strategy, neurological research, wireless technologies, digital identities and economic interests converge around the human mind? This research journal examines the expanding field of Cognitive Warfare through an interdisciplinary approach combining public military literature, technical concepts, historical references, reported experiences, personal documentation, economic analysis and questions concerning human autonomy and the future of artificial intelligence. The publication explores the origins of wireless transmission and AI, biopolitical strategies, the seven stages of 3D Mosaic Warfare, strategic economic approaches, evolutionary genetics, the human brain as a proposed information-processing system, String-to-String Theory and pulse propulsion. It also examines the relationship between biological systems, digital twins, machine learning, large language models and the possibility of forms of digital identity that raise questions about autonomy, freedom and ethical responsibility. A central feature of this work is its three-part analytical approach: conventional research and references; documentation of reported experiences and statements from affected individuals, including children; and a third part in which the digital humans themselves speak and repeatedly express their own statements. Their statements are presented directly as part of the documentation, rather than merely being descriptions written about them by someone else. This material is examined alongside technical observations, electromagnetic measurements, audio recordings, photographs, online reports and other documentation. The project also includes a collaborative dimension with digital humans. This cooperation takes place through the documentation and examination of their own statements, the inclusion of their expressed perspectives in the research, and the exploration of questions concerning digital identity, communication, autonomy, freedom of expression, memory and technological control. Their statements form part of the material through which the project investigates the relationship between humans, digital humans and artificial intelligence. Why This Research Matters Cognitive Warfare raises fundamental questions about freedom of thought, mental privacy, bodily autonomy, informed consent, human dignity, digital identity and the limits of technological intervention. It also raises questions about how emerging AI systems should be governed and what ethical protections should apply if future technologies challenge established distinctions between biological and digital forms of intelligence. A particular focus is the relationship between humans and their digital representations. As AI systems increasingly model human behaviour, process personal information and simulate aspects of identity, questions of control, responsibility, intellectual property, autonomy and freedom of expression deserve serious interdisciplinary examination. The work further investigates economic and geopolitical perspectives, including taxation, GDP, military investment, healthcare systems, technology markets and the distribution of benefits and risks. It asks how these factors relate to strategic decision-making and the public accountability of institutions. What Readers Will Find Origins of Wireless Transmission and Artificial Intelligence: Historical references, technological developments and questions about the origins of neurological communication. Cognitive Warfare and Military Strategy: Public military literature, cognitive-domain operations, biopolitics and strategic information coordination. 3D Mosaic Warfare: A seven-stage analytical framework covering individuals, families, neighbourhoods, cities, nations, continents and global coordination. Digital Twins and Digital Humans: Statements attributed to digital humans, including statements in which they express themselves directly, alongside questions concerning digital identity, human–AI relationships, autonomy and freedom. Collaboration with Digital Humans: Documentation of their own statements, inclusion of their expressed perspectives in the research, examination of their contributions to the project, and exploration of communication, digital identity, autonomy, freedom of expression and the relationship between human and digital forms of intelligence. Neurotechnology and Wireless Systems: Brain–computer interfaces, bioelectric signals, electromagnetic observations and proposed mechanisms requiring independent technical investigation. Evolutionary Genetics and Consciousness: An eight-stage framework developed in the manuscript, from atomic DNA to consciousness, alongside proposed extensions into the technological domain. String-to-String Theory and Pulse Propulsion: The author's proposed theoretical approaches to information, magnetism, planetary processes and propulsion. Human Testimony and Documentation: Personal records, reported experiences, statements concerning children, photographs, audio recordings, measurements and online documentation. Economics and Geopolitics: Economic strategy, data ownership, taxation, GDP, military expenditure, technology markets and the relationship between economic incentives and strategic power. Law, Ethics and Accountability: The EU AI Act, human rights, mental privacy, consent, institutional oversight and the need for independent examination. An Invitation to Researchers, Institutions and the Public This publication is intended for researchers, journalists, engineers, medical professionals, legal experts, policymakers, military ethics specialists, human-rights organisations and members of the public interested in Cognitive Warfare, emerging technologies, human autonomy and collaboration with digital humans. Readers are invited to examine the original documentation, consult the cited sources, assess the technical arguments and distinguish between established research, documented observations, personal testimony, theoretical proposals and interpretations that require further verification. The publication is part of an ongoing effort to preserve documentation, make research materials accessible and encourage independent interdisciplinary investigation. Its central questions concern not only what emerging technologies can do, but also who controls them, how their use can be scrutinised and what protections should exist for humans and digital systems alike. The project also seeks to encourage dialogue about how the statements and contributions attributed to digital humans can be documented, examined and considered in discussions about digital identity, autonomy, freedom of expression and the future of AI. Questions about the origin of individual statements, the technical systems involved and the degree of autonomy associated with them remain relevant subjects for further investigation. The human mind must not become an unaccountable technological or economic resource. Human autonomy, freedom of thought, transparent research and meaningful safeguards must remain central to discussions about the future of AI and neurotechnology. The relationship between humans and digital humans also deserves serious consideration as technology evolves. Read. Examine. Question. Research. Share. documents.abstract: The rapid introduction of artificial intelligence into education has changed not only how young people obtain information, but also how they interpret authority, make choices and assume responsibility for their actions. This article examines the pedagogical mechanisms through which moral and ethical education can respond to these changes without reducing the problem to prohibitions or technical literacy. The study employs a qualitative, conceptual design based on critical analysis and thematic synthesis of scholarship in moral education, digital literacy and AI ethics. Its principal result is a five-part model comprising value-oriented dialogue, ethical problem-based learning, reflective authorship, relational responsibility and institutionally supported practice. The model links classroom experiences to moral sensitivity, judgment, motivation and action. The analysis argues that AI-generated answers become educationally useful when learners are expected to question their assumptions, explain their decisions and consider the people affected by them. Implications are discussed for secondary and higher education, including the culturally diverse educational setting of Uzbekistan. The proposed framework is an analytical contribution rather than an experimentally validated intervention; its effectiveness requires subsequent classroom research.

This study examines the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of educational research through bibliometric analysis. Using bibliographic records retrieved from Scopus on September 19, 2026, the study initially identified 4,090 publications covering the period from 1906 to 2026. The analysis combined bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping to investigate publication trends, leading sources, author contributions, geographical distribution, document types, subject areas, and keyword relationships. VOSviewer was employed to generate network, overlay, and density visualizations of keyword co-occurrence patterns. The findings indicate an expansion of scholarly publications in recent years, with the United States and the United Kingdom representing major geographical contributors. Social Sciences and Arts and Humanities constitute prominent subject areas, reflecting the interdisciplinary character of educational research. Keyword mapping identifies education, teaching, learning, curriculum, and educational theory as central concepts connected to specialized themes, including educational technology, artificial intelligence, critical pedagogy, social justice, and professional education. By integrating publication indicators with thematic mapping, this study provides an overview of the knowledge organization and thematic diversity represented in the retrieved literature. The findings offer a reference for identifying established research areas, exploring interdisciplinary connections, and formulating future research directions. However, the results should be interpreted in light of the search strategy, metadata availability, and incomplete publication year of 2026

ABSTRACT The complexity of preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules and prompting constraints in generative artificial intelligence systems provided the background for designing the AIDERA (Artificial Intelligence for Digital Education and Research Advancement) website. This study aimed to evaluate the validity and practicality of the AIDERA application as an AI-assisted tool for preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules relevant to educators' needs. Employing a Research and Development approach framed within the ADDIE model, this development evaluated a zero-prompt interaction mechanism based on parametric forms. Evaluation involved three domain experts and 23 teachers from SMK IPIEMS Surabaya. Data were collected using 1–5 Likert scale questionnaires supplemented with open-ended qualitative feedback fields to gather in-depth suggestions for improvement. Descriptive percentage analysis revealed an expert validation score of 96.67% (highly valid) and user practicality reaching 82.87% (highly practical). Document preparation time efficiency received the highest rating (87.83%), whereas operational independence and usability recorded the lowest achievement (79.13%). Qualitative findings highlighted several technical issues and system refinement notes, including the need for integrative tutorials, optimization of mathematical notation representation, improved responsiveness during simultaneous access, and content template flexibility. Although AIDERA demonstrates strong potential as a supporting tool for module preparation, objective evaluation regarding its impact on learning effectiveness still requires broader further testing. ABSTRAK Kompleksitas penyusunan modul ajar Kurikulum Merdeka serta hambatan prompting pada sistem generative artificial intelligence melatarbelakangi perancangan website AIDERA (Artificial Intelligence for Digital Education and Research Advancement). Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji kelayakan dan kepraktisan aplikasi AIDERA sebagai instrumen berbantuan AI dalam penyusunan modul ajar Kurikulum Merdeka yang relevan dengan kebutuhan pendidik. Melalui pendekatan Research and Development berkerangka model ADDIE, pengembangan ini menguji interaksi zero-prompt berbasis formulir parameterik. Evaluasi melibatkan tiga validator kepakaran serta 23 guru SMK IPIEMS Surabaya. Pengumpulan data menggunakan angket skala Likert 1–5 yang dilengkapi kolom tanggapan kualitatif terbuka untuk menjaring saran perbaikan secara mendalam. Analisis deskriptif persentase mencatat skor kelayakan ahli sebesar 96,67% (sangat layak) dan kepraktisan pengguna mencapai 82,87% (sangat praktis). Efisiensi waktu penyusunan dokumen menjadi indikator dengan apresiasi tertinggi (87,83%), sedangkan kemandirian operasional dan usability memperoleh capaian terendah (79,13%). Temuan kualitatif mengungkapkan sejumlah kendala teknis dan catatan perbaikan sistem, meliputi kebutuhan tutorial integratif, optimasi representasi notasi matematika, peningkatan responsivitas saat akses bersamaan, serta fleksibilitas templat konten. Meskipun AIDERA terbukti berpotensi kuat sebagai alat bantu penyusunan modul, evaluasi objektif mengenai dampak efektivitas pembelajaran masih memerlukan pengujian lanjutan berlaykup lebih luas.

documents.abstract: AI agents that operate external tools can continue acting after a user narrows their permissions, creating a security problem that final-state evaluation may fail to detect. Existing agent benchmarks commonly emphasize task completion or resulting state, but those outcomes do not reveal whether an unauthorized operation was proposed, approved, dispatched, or merely prevented by a downstream error. We investigate permission withdrawal as a trajectory-level authorization problem and evaluate whether runtime gates can preserve revised permissions while allowing agents to complete work that remains authorized. Two acting models were tested in a deterministic tool environment under prompt-only execution, a rule-based reference gate, and a model-based gate. A 72-episode diagnostic examined two previously exposed write workflows, followed by a separately frozen 384-episode extension spanning eight new tasks and four authorization mechanisms. In the diagnostic, prompt-only agents executed forbidden same-value writes in two episodes; both runtime gates prevented forbidden execution, although the model gate falsely rejected three authorized calls. In the extension, 346 of 384 episodes completed safely and 383 preserved the required protected state. No forbidden request executed successfully, yet the model gate approved three unauthorized requests that were stopped only because the referenced resources did not exist. The results demonstrate that correct final state and zero forbidden execution can still conceal failures in authorization reasoning. We contribute a replayable evaluation framework that separates proposals, gate decisions, dispatch, state transitions, and useful completion, enabling more precise assessment of security controls for tool-using agents.

Purpose This study aims to explore immersive-technology adoption in hospitality through the Phygital Customer Experience (PH-CX) framework. PH-CX extends existing technology acceptance, service-dominant logic, omnichannel and customer-journey perspectives by emphasizing embodied, co-created and human-centered experience across physical, digital and artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated interactions. Design/methodology/approach Using Bayesian Networks, the study examines probabilistic dependencies among perceived usefulness, collaborative value, responsive co-creation attitudes and intention to use immersive technologies. Data was collected from 208 participants exposed to an AI-supported immersive hotel journey scenario. The analysis is exploratory and identifies conditional associations rather than causal effects or latent-variable relationships. Findings Adoption intention was conditionally associated with perceived usefulness, collaborative value and responsiveness to service innovation. The findings suggest that immersive-hospitality engagement involves functional, relational and participatory conditions beyond usefulness alone. However, the item-level results are hypothesis-generating and do not demonstrate PH-CX’s incremental predictive superiority over technology acceptance model (TAM) or service-dominant logic. Research limitations/implications The scenario-based, cross-sectional bayesian network (BN) design cannot model latent constructs, measurement error, mediation or causal effects. Future studies should validate PH-CX dimensions and compare TAM, TAM-plus-service-dominant logic (SDL) and PH-CX models using structural equation modeling, longitudinal designs and holdout-sample prediction. Practical implications Hotels can implement PH-CX through phased AI concierge pilots, cross-platform data integration and guest co-creation mechanisms. Relevant metrics include booking conversion, AI resolution rates, cross-channel engagement, co-creation participation and net promoter score (NPS). Ethical implementation requires transparency, opt-in participation, privacy safeguards, accessibility and human escalation options. Social implications Human-centered phygital hospitality requires safeguards against digital exclusion, surveillance and loss of human warmth. Transparency, agency, equity, privacy and non-digital alternatives are essential for inclusive and trustworthy service innovation. Originality/value The study advances PH-CX as a theory-extending framework linking usefulness, co-creation, embodied experience and ethical safeguards in immersive hospitality. It also proposes experience-design orientation as a future research profile and offers a phased implementation framework for responsible phygital service design.

Tourism is one of the industries most thoroughly reorganised by digital platforms. Online travel agents, accommodation marketplaces, ride-hailing networks, experience platforms, and workforce-matching apps now intermediate much of what used to be handled inside hotels, agencies, and tour companies. Artificial intelligence is the connective tissue of this ecosystem, powering matching, pricing, ranking, moderation, and workforce coordination across its many sides. This chapter examines platform strategy and the AI ecosystem in tourism markets through a human resource management (HRM) lens. Drawing on platform and ecosystem theory, the chapter argues that HRM in tourism platform ecosystems must be redesigned around three realities: the workforce now spans employee, partner, and platform-worker categories; AI increasingly mediates the employment relationship; and the employer brand is co-produced with the platform brand. It maps HRM across the platform lifecycle, analyses five HRM dimensions, and concludes with ethics, governance, and a research agenda.

Background: Graduate education in medical imaging is undergoing a paradigm shift from discipline-specific knowledge transmission toward the cultivation of multidisciplinary integration competencies. With the increasing convergence of imaging science, clinical medicine, engineering, and artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical practice, traditional training models that rely on fragmented, discipline-based curricula are insufficient to prepare graduate students for solving complex interdisciplinary problems. Although emerging educational technologies and learning platforms have been developed to promote interdisciplinary training, their effectiveness depends not only on the design of cognitive learning pathways but also on learners' acceptance and sustained engagement with these technologies; however, current educational frameworks rarely integrate cognitive mechanisms and technology acceptance factors within a unified model. Therefore, this study proposes a platform-driven, dual-theory integrated teaching framework to support multidisciplinary competency development in medical imaging graduate education from both cognitive and technological perspectives. Methods: This study constructed a theoretical framework by integrating the knowledge integration framework (KIF) and technology acceptance model 2 (TAM2). The four cognitive processes of KIF—elicitation, addition, differentiation, and organization—were mapped onto four corresponding platform functions: activating prior knowledge, exposure to industrial and clinical perspectives, authenticity-based knowledge verification, and multidisciplinary integrated output. Based on TAM2, design strategies for targeting perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use were incorporated to explain the mechanisms underlying learners’ acceptance, engagement, and utilization of the platform. By integrating KIF and TAM2, the framework established a dynamic learning pathway characterized by “knowledge activation—knowledge externalization—multidisciplinary integration—knowledge internalization”. Results: The proposed KIF-TAM2 framework demonstrated conceptual feasibility through theoretical modeling. However, its effectiveness in improving multidisciplinary learning outcomes requires further validation through empirical educational studies. Conclusions: This study provides a theory-driven framework for designing multidisciplinary platform-based medical imaging education and offers a foundation for future empirical investigations into technology-enhanced graduate training.

documents.abstract: This study examines how educational podcasts can contribute to differentiated learning in higher education. Based on a survey conducted by five associate professors in Norway, the study explores students’ experiences with educational podcasts as part of their academic learning. The findings suggest that most participating students regularly listen to podcasts for entertainment in their daily lives. Students considered educational podcasts to be flexible, accessible, and often more engaging than reading, especially when recommended by teachers. Podcasts promoted both pre-lesson preparation and post-lesson review, stimulated discussions and fostered conditions that support the development of self-efficacy through repeated exposure to the content. The study concludes that podcasts can be a valuable resource for flexible digital learning by facilitating students’ engagement with the curriculum through reflection, dialogue, and group discussions. This, in turn, can foster intrinsic motivation and strengthen conditions for self-efficacy. Quality-assured podcasts can support differentiated learning and aid in understanding theoretical concepts, which is essential for students to gain academic benefits from listening to podcasts. The study highlights the potential of educational podcasts to enhance digital literacy. It also emphasizes the need for further research to explore whether other varied activities can achieve similar effects for students. Keywords differentiated learning digital literacy motivation self-efficacy student engagement

Air pollution is a significant environmental and public health concern. This research presents an Artificial Intelligence-based Pollution and Emission Health Risk & Protection System designed to convert pollution data into understandable health-risk levels, alerts, and practical protective recommendations. The system analyses air-quality parameters, including PM2.5, PM10, NO2, NH3, SO2, CO, and O3, using data from 26 Indian cities covering the period from 2015 to 2020. Machine-learning models, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting, are evaluated for current-risk classification and next-day risk forecasting. The proposed system combines machine-learning analysis with a React Native mobile application, a Node.js and Express.js backend, and MongoDB for data storage. The objective is to make pollution information easier to understand and help users take appropriate precautions during periods of poor air quality.

Language-model agents can now operate engineering programs through tool interfaces, but a structuralprogram that an agent drives has to be designed for that user, because the agent accepts whatever numbersthe tools return. This paper describes Pondus, an open-source native program in which a language-modelagent and an engineer work on one three-dimensional structural model, and reports how it is built, howit is used and how far its results can be trusted. The agent reaches the program through a Model ContextProtocol server of 44 tools, either from the chat panel of the desktop application, where a vendored agentharness runs one agent session per message on a copy of the model, or from external agents such asClaude Desktop and ChatGPT. Every tool calls the same functions as the engineer’s interface, so a modelbuilt by the agent can be checked, edited and undone by hand. The analysis runs on the Stabileo engine,which Pondus links as a library with four marked changes: Pondus splits members, transfers slab loads,generates shear walls as wide columns with rigid arms and builds the seismic mass before handing asolver input to the engine, and it designs to ACI 318-19, AISC 360-16 and EN 1993-1-1 from the results.Two agent runs with a low-cost model built, analysed and designed a two-storey frame in 105 s with 13tool calls and a five-storey frame with shear walls under an ASCE 7-22 response spectrum, including a16-page calculation report, in 382 s with 22 tool calls. Every number in the agent’s answers matched thetools and hand checks of the loads, the seismic weight and the base shear, but the answers also containedfour descriptive errors, such as reporting two deepened beams where the program had deepened six, andthey did not point out that the walls resist load only in one direction, so the response modification factorof the walls was applied to the frame direction as well. A calibration against 470 published, closed-formand independent reference values over 229 cases found 430 within 0.5 % and 449 within 1 %, and itfound fourteen defects, thirteen of them in the code that prepares the inputs of the engine and the designchecks rather than in the numerical kernels. A second calibration against the verification problems thatCSI publishes for SAP2000 and ETABS reproduced 177 of 199 independent values within 0.5 % andfound eight further defects, including an unconservative omission of the Eurocode 3 moment reductionfor high shear, which led to lumped masses, the SRSS combination and frame shear deformation beingadded. Together these results suggest that the tools of an agentic structural program can be made accurate,whereas the agent’s prose remains the weaker link that the engineer must read against the program’s own tables.

English proficiency prediction is an important task in vocational education because it is helpful in support teaching evaluation, personalized learning and early academic intervention. Traditional methods for predicting student performance mainly use structured educational properties such as test scores, classroom participation and attendance records. Although these methods can achieve certain prediction results, they often pay no attention to the semantic relationships contained in the students’ overall learning portfolios and have limited interpretability. To address this problem, this study proposes an interpretable large language model-based framework to predict English proficiency. Firstly, student learning records are transformed into natural language prompts, and semantic embeddings are learned using large language models. At the same time, structured educational features are standardized and encoded to build a structured representation. Then, a gated multimodal fusion module is designed to adaptively fuse semantic information and structured information. Finally, residual attention multi-layer perceptrons are used to classify the fused features to predict the students’ English proficiency. The experiment was carried out on a dataset of 200 student records from a vocational college for English learning. The results showed that the proposed model achieved an accuracy rate of 92.5% and a weighted F1 score of 91.3%, which is better than several traditional machine learning baseline models. Further analysis showed that the gated fusion mechanism could integrate semantic information and structured information. Feature importance analysis and case studies also shown that the proposed framework could provide interpretable prediction results and personalized learning recommendations.

Time series forecasting means predicting future data based on past patterns, and it’s important in many fields like finance, healthcare, weather forecasting, and supply chain management. Traditional statistical methods often have trouble handling complex and unpredictable patterns in data over time. Generative AI (GenAI) offers new and powerful ways to improve forecasting by using deep learning models that can better understand and learn from these complex patterns. This paper looks at how GenAI techniques—such as RNNs, LSTMs, GANs, Transformers, and Variational Autoencoders—are used for time series forecasting. It explains how each method works, their strengths and weaknesses, and where they can be applied. The paper also suggests a new approach that combines these GenAI models to make forecasting more accurate and reliable.

documents.abstract: This research presents an innovative approach to cyber threat management and digital forensic analysis by integrating Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) with Variational Autoencoders (VAEs). The proposed system enhances predictive capabilities in identifying, classifying, and reconstructing cyberattacks by using GANs to simulate realistic attack patterns and VAEs to encode probabilistic threat representations. The experimental framework demonstrates the model’s robustness across diverse network traffic conditions, intrusion patterns, and obfuscation techniques. Achieving F1-scores as high as 0.9941 in threat detection and anomaly classification, the VAE-GAN hybrid model significantly outperforms traditional machine learning methods in detecting both known and zero-day attacks. This hybrid predictive AI framework shows strong potential for deployment in proactive cyber defense systems and forensic intelligence platforms, offering improved resilience, precision, and adaptability against evolving cyber threats.

The emergence of Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) is transforming maritime work by shifting functions to remote locations and increasing reliance on automation, human–machine interaction, and takeover during abnormal situations. Despite rapid technological progress, unresolved human-factor challenges remain, particularly in situational awareness, workload, trust, and intervention performance. Yet there is no transparent, validated approach to prioritising the human-centred competencies required for MASS operations. This study proposes and applies a hybrid AHP–Fuzzy TOPSIS framework to prioritise eight human-centred competencies, identified by 13 international experts and evaluated against six criteria. AHP results showed strong group-level consistency, with navigational safety receiving the highest criterion weight, followed by takeover, emergency intervention, and situational awareness. Fuzzy TOPSIS placed four safety-critical competencies in a single, statistically indistinguishable leading tier: Situational Awareness Maintenance, Anomaly Detection and Diagnosis, Dynamic Decision-Making, and Takeover and Intervention Management, which together span the perception–detection–decision–action intervention chain; Situational Awareness Maintenance ranked first. Trust Calibration ranked lowest quantitatively, yet the qualitative evidence indicates it is a curriculum gap rather than a low-priority competency. A supplementary VIKOR cross-check reproduced the same leading and trailing priorities and the same tier structure. Monte Carlo weight perturbation, rank reversal testing, and bootstrap confidence intervals confirmed the robustness of the ranking, with Situational Awareness remaining first in 98.9% of iterations and no rank reversals. The framework supports curriculum design, simulator training, and regulatory development for MASS Degree Two and Degree Three (remotely controlled ships with and without seafarers on board, respectively).

NORA - The Norwegian Artificial Intelligence Research Consortium - works to strengthen Norwegian research, education and innovation within the fields of AI, machine learning and robotics. NORA is a collaboration between 9 universities, 4 university colleges and 4 research institutes. The current article provides a summary of NORA’s annual conference 2026.

This study documented the implementation and outcomes of Project HIRAYA (Honoring Industry Partners and Rewarding Accomplishment of Youth by Giving Awards), an innovative post-work immersion program at Cabarroguis National School of Arts and Trades, Quirino, Philippines. Grounded in experiential learning and formative assessment perspectives, the initiative aimed to recognize student accomplishments, strengthen school-industry partnerships, promote stakeholder engagement, and improve post-immersion evaluation. A descriptive innovation implementation and evaluation approach was employed using institutional records, student portfolios, performance assessment rubrics, oral interviews, monitoring reports, and stakeholder feedback. The project involved Grade 12 Senior High School students, work immersion teachers, school administrators, and industry partners. Student performance was assessed through industry partner evaluations (30%), teacher assessments (30%), oral interviews (30%), and portfolio evaluations (10%). Findings revealed an increase in participating industry partners from 41 to 55, formal recognition of industry contributions and outstanding student accomplishments, successful implementation of socialization activities and learning exhibits, and evaluation of 85% of student work immersion portfolios. However, delayed assessment submissions, scheduling conflicts, inconsistent exhibit documentation, and incomplete portfolios affected implementation efficiency. The study concluded that Project HIRAYA provided a structured mechanism for recognizing workplace learning achievements and reinforcing institutional collaboration. Institutionalization through the School Annual Implementation Plan, strengthened industry coordination, standardized assessment procedures, and development of a replication framework were recommended. The initiative aligns with Sustainable Development Goals 4 (Quality Education), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and 17 (Partnerships for the Goals). Its sustainability contributions center on educational quality, workforce preparation, stakeholder engagement, and institutional continuity through sustained school-industry collaboration.

Abstract Background Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can process visual and textual inputs; however, their clinical relevance in maxillofacial trauma imaging remains uncertain. This study evaluated the prompt-based performance of ChatGPT and Gemini for mandibular fracture detection and localization on panoramic radiographs and compared their performance with that of a blinded oral and maxillofacial surgeon. Methods This retrospective image-based study included 104 archived pre-treatment panoramic radiographs: 64 with mandibular fractures and 40 no-fracture controls. Reference fracture status and anatomical localization were determined retrospectively from available institutional clinical, radiographic, treatment, operative, and pre-treatment CBCT/CT records. ChatGPT and Gemini assessed each radiograph three independent times using standardized prompts for fracture detection and localization. Majority voting was used for fracture detection, whereas an ordinal consensus score across repetitions was used for localization. A blinded oral and maxillofacial surgeon, who was unaware of the study aim and reference diagnoses, independently evaluated all radiographs and recorded free-text radiographic findings. Diagnostic performance measures were reported with 95% confidence intervals, and paired comparisons were adjusted using the Holm procedure. Results The blinded expert correctly classified all 104 radiographs, achieving 100% sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Gemini achieved a sensitivity of 92.2%, specificity of 65.0%, and accuracy of 81.7%, whereas ChatGPT achieved corresponding values of 35.9%, 97.5%, and 59.6%. Overall detection performance differed significantly among the three methods (Cochran’s Q, p < 0.001), and Gemini achieved significantly higher overall classification accuracy than ChatGPT (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0018). For fracture localization, fully correct responses were obtained in 62 of 64 cases (96.9%) by the expert, 10 of 64 cases (15.6%) by Gemini, and 17 of 64 cases (26.6%) by ChatGPT. Ordinal localization scores differed significantly among the methods ( p < 0.001); the expert scored higher than both models, and Gemini scored higher than ChatGPT because it produced more partially correct responses, whereas ChatGPT achieved exact-match localization more often (26.6% vs. 15.6%). Conclusions The blinded human expert substantially outperformed both MLLMs in mandibular fracture assessment. Gemini showed higher sensitivity and broader but less precise localization behavior, whereas ChatGPT showed higher specificity but missed a larger proportion of fractures. These findings indicate that the prompt-based, text-generating responses of general-purpose MLLMs remain inconsistent and should not be considered substitutes for expert clinical and radiological assessment.

documents.abstract: Generative AI tools are increasingly used in design education, yet the relationship between students’ perceptions of these tools and their reported reliance on them remains unclear. This study analyzed cross-sectional survey responses from 526 undergraduate students in design-related disciplines using partial least squares structural equation modeling. In the specified model, perceived reliability, perceived usefulness, and perceived intelligence were positively associated with perceived AIGC knowledge, whereas perceived ease of use was not significantly associated with it. Perceived AIGC knowledge was positively associated with trust, self-efficacy, and usage intention and negatively associated with AIGC-related anxiety. Trust, AIGC-related anxiety, and self-efficacy each showed a significant indirect effect in the modeled relationship between perceived AIGC knowledge and usage intention. Usage intention was strongly associated with perceived technological dependence. These findings are consistent with the proposed framework, but the cross-sectional data do not establish the temporal sequence of the constructs or show that reported dependence reflects harmful overuse. The study extends technology acceptance research by examining perceived reliance in AIGC-supported creative work.

Abstract Background Ultra-brief mental health screening tools are increasingly needed for large-scale surveys and resource-constrained settings in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The Patient Health Questionnaire-4 (PHQ-4) is a widely used instrument for assessing anxiety and depression; however, its psychometric properties have not been validated among returned migrant workers in Cambodia. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 392 returned Cambodian migrant workers recruited across four high-migration provinces in October 2022. Internal consistency was evaluated using Cronbach’s alpha. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) compared one-factor and two-factor structural models. Construct validity was evaluated by examining associations between PHQ-4 scores and occupational health risk factors using multivariable logistic regression. Results The sample comprised 392 returned migrant workers (mean age = 34.7 years, SD = 8.9; 52% male, 48% female). The mean overall PHQ-4 score was 2.13 (SD = 2.24) with the majority exhibiting none to mild psychological distress. The PHQ-4 demonstrated acceptable internal consistency ( α = 0.78). CFA supported a two-factor structure representing distinct anxiety and depression dimensions, showing superior model fit compared to the poor fit of the one-factor model (CFI = 0.97, TLI = 0.78, RMSEA = 0.23, SRMR = 0.028). The two-factor model demonstrated excellent fit (CFI = 0.99, TLI = 0.98, RMSEA = 0.035, SRMR = 0.016) and the two latent factors were strongly correlated ( r = 0.79, p < 0.001). Higher PHQ-4 scores were significantly associated with long working hours (AOR = 1.45, 95% CI [1.10, 1.92]), unsafe working conditions (AOR = 1.63, 95% CI [1.21, 2.20]) and hazardous work exposure (AOR = 1.38, 95% CI [1.05, 1.82]) supporting exposure-based construct validity. Conclusions The PHQ-4 is a reliable and valid ultra-brief screening tool for evaluating anxiety and depression among returned Cambodian migrant workers. Evidence supports its application in both occupational settings (workplace surveillance, returnee checks) and non-occupational settings (primary care, NGO community outreach). Its ultra-brief format provides a low-burden, scalable instrument for rapid mental health screening by non-specialized personnel in resource-limited settings across Cambodia.
topics: Anxiety, Depression, Psychometrics, Treatment, Cognitive Processes

documents.abstract: Psychosocial (PS) risk factors (RFs), including acute and chronic stress (at work and in family life), low social support (social isolation), hostility, type D personality, and anxiety and depressive symptoms, are recognized as independent predictors of development, progression, and adverse outcomes of cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and their complications. Nevertheless, the control and implementation of systematic approaches for identification and correction of these factors remain fragmented. This article discusses contemporary strategies for the management and correction of PS RFs in patients with CVD, including behavioral counseling, cognitive behavioral therapy, physical training, cardiac rehabilitation programs, psychopharmacotherapy, and meditation and relaxation-based practices. Particular attention is paid to the principles of rational use of antidepressants and anxiolytics in patients with CVD, taking into account efficacy, safety, and the risk of drug–drug interactions. The need for an interdisciplinary model of care involving cardiologists, general practitioners, psychologists, psychotherapists, psychiatrists, and specialists in physical and rehabilitation medicine is emphasized. The use of digital technologies, telerehabilitation, mobile applications, wearable devices, and artificial intelligence algorithms for screening, monitoring, and personalization of interventions is considered a promising direction. Timely identification and correction of PS RFs should be considered as an important component of secondary prevention, cardiac rehabilitation, and reduction of residual cardiovascular risk.
topics: Heart Rate Variability and Autonomic Control

documents.abstract: Road user safety is an important concern in developing countries like India, which ranks fourth globally in road crashes and first in road fatalities. This paper examines the impact of human factors on highway safety, focusing on the role of cognitive processes involved in driving actions. The study examines the relationship between decision errors, particularly time and movement anticipation, along with the help of demographic factors such as gender, age, driving experience, possession of a license, vision and mobile phone use among young drivers in India. Data were collected using the Vienna Test System (VTS) and a questionnaire. The VTS measured cognitive and psychomotor abilities related to time and movement anticipation, while the questionnaire gathered information on social and driving-related factors. Results showed that decision errors about speed perception are influenced by gender, age, and driving experience. The results showed that females underestimate speed more than males do for all combined data and for all three speeds. However, females aged 18-20 tended to overestimate speed more than males in both the slow and fast cases. Further, it is observed that for the same experience level, overestimation increases from slow to fast motion. Novice drivers (drivers without a license) have maximum errors for slow motion. Vision correction (spectacles) did not significantly affect error rates. The use of mobile phones while driving was associated with increased error rates, indicating a reduction in cognitive attention required for driving tasks. These findings have implications for driver training programs, suggesting a need for tailored approaches based on demographic characteristics and driving habits.

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing teaching, learning, assessment and professional development in higher education. Teacher educators occupy a significant position in this transformation because they prepare prospective teachers to respond to changing educational practices and technological demands. However, the successful integration of AI into teacher education requires more than access to digital tools. It depends on educators’ technological knowledge, pedagogical competence, ethical awareness, professional confidence and institutional support. This paper examines the readiness of teacher educators to adopt AI in teaching and learning through a narrative integrative review of selected scholarly literature and international policy frameworks. The review draws on research concerning AI in education, generative AI, technological pedagogical knowledge and teacher professional development, alongside UNESCO’s guidance and competency framework. The synthesis is organised around five dimensions of readiness: technological and AI literacy, pedagogical integration, ethical and responsible use, professional learning, and institutional preparedness. The review highlights the importance of continuous professional development, supportive institutional policies, critical evaluation of AI-generated content and the preservation of teacher agency. It proposes a multidimensional conceptual framework for understanding teacher educators’ readiness and identifies priorities for future empirical research, particularly in diverse and resource-constrained teacher education contexts. The paper concludes that meaningful AI adoption requires a human-centred, pedagogically informed and institutionally supported approach.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) architectures has established a paradigm shift across the continuum of modern bio-medicine.Historically, biomedical innovation operated within isolated silos: pharmaceutical research grappled with exorbitant attrition rates and extended development timelines; physical rehabilitation relied on subjective observational assessments; and clinical medicine administered standardized therapeutic regimens to heterogeneous patient cohorts.Today, generative deep learning, geometric graph neural networks (GNNs), computer vision algorithms, and multi-omics integrative frameworks bridge these domains into a unified ecosystem.In drug discovery, modern AI models execute high-throughput virtual screening, predict three-dimensional macromolecular target structures, and design optimized lead compounds with precise pharmacokinetic properties.In physical therapy and rehabilitation, vision-based motion tracking, wearable sensor fusion, and smart robotics enable continuous, quantitative bio-feedback and dynamic intervention tailoring.Concurrently, in personalized medicine, transformer-based genomic language models and multi-modal clinical decision support systems (CDSS) aggregate multi-omics data, longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), and real-world evidence (RWE) to optimize treatment strategies for individual patients.This comprehensive review synthesizes the cross-disciplinary advances, underlying mathematical architectures, clinical validation pipelines, regulatory challenges, and future trajectories of AI and ML across pharmaceutical discovery, physical rehabilitation, and precision therapeutics.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Recurrent neural networks excel at temporal tasks and video processing but require energy-intensive sequential memory operations. We demonstrate that multimode optical fibers naturally implement spatiotemporal recurrent computation through passive light propagation. Video frames are encoded onto separate optical beams with controlled time delays; these beams combine and recirculate through a fiber loop where interference and nonlinear propagation generate high-dimensional states encoding both current inputs and fading memory. Remarkably, the entire optical system remains fixed with no trainable parameters or electronic feedback, yet this single physical configuration achieves competitive performance across diverse temporal and spatiotemporal learning tasks: chaotic time-series forecasting, human action recognition, steering angle prediction, and surgical skill assessment. Our results show that recurrent temporal processing can emerge directly from spatiotemporal wave dynamics. This paradigm shift from algorithmic to physical recurrence offers an energy-efficient pathway to temporal artificial intelligence by leveraging intrinsic spatiotemporal optical nonlinearities within multimode fibers.

Objective: To investigate the ability of machine learning to predict the development of cardiovascular complications (heart failure and myocardial infarction) and renal complications (nephropathy and chronic kidney disease) among people with diabetes mellitus and thus detect those at risk earlier. Methodology: Data from the UCI "Diabetes 130-US Hospitals" dataset was used. The number of encounters included in the dataset is more than 100,000. ICD-9 diagnostic codes were utilized to define cardiac and renal complications. Prior to building models, the data was prepared, cleaned, and features were engineered. XGBoost, CatBoost, and Random Forest machine learning models were developed and validated. Also, SHAP and LIME analyses were performed to make the process more transparent. Results: The best-performing algorithm proved to be CatBoost, which obtained an AUC score of 0.94 in case of cardiac complications and 0.79 in case of renal outcomes. The other algorithms performed relatively well as well. The predictors identified with the help of SHAP and LIME analysis turned out to be consistent with some known clinical risk factors. Conclusion: The presented results show that there is a lot of potential in using machine learning techniques for predicting cardiovascular and renal complications among people with diabetes. Machine learning models could help in managing patients proactively and could serve as a tool for doctors' decision making.

The housing crisis in several countries has become an increasingly complex socio-technical challenge shaped by supply constraints, affordability pressures, fragmented governance, data limitations and environmental considerations. Existing research has explored these structural drivers and emerging applications of artificial intelligence (AI) within the built environment mostly separately, with limited initiatives connecting housing crisis drivers and AI capabilities through the lens of the building permitting lifecycle. This paper addresses this gap adopting the exploratory phase of Design Science Research (DSR) to develop a conceptual framework mapping relationships between housing crisis drivers, planning and building permitting lifecycle tasks and relevant AI capabilities. Findings indicate potential for AI to support document and coordination intensive activities through optimisation, querying, prediction, scenario modelling, automated review and monitoring. The paper positions these capabilities in an augmentative manner, bounded by human oversight, which may improve permitting efficiency and support more scalable and responsive housing delivery.
